transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Nora Patel (Redwood) / Ravi Menon, Aisha Khan, Diego Ruiz, Leah Park (Cinder)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot cache numbers (prefix vs KV hit rates), decisions on prompt normalization, and agreement on next benchmark steps. Some noisy audio; a few auto-transcription glitches (model names, acronyms).

Topics:
- KV cache hit-rate trends (last 7 days)
- Prefix caching behavior and eviction patterns
- Prompt reuse and canonicalization strategy
- Batch size trade-offs and latency impact
- Security question: KMS & log retention for private deploys

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 45 minute sync. I think we have Ravi and Aisha from Cinder, thanks for making time. 
[00:12] Ravi Menon: Yep, thanks Maya. We jumped in with the pilot last week, saw some promising hit rates but a few spikes in tail latency. Diego's got the SRE context.
[00:22] Diego Ruiz: Morning. Yeah the tail seen at ~99th percentile went up during our afternoon traffic window, about 30% higher than baseline on Tuesday.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Ok, that's helpful. We pulled the KV metrics and prefix reuse. Over the past 7 days KV global hit-rate is about 54% average, but prefix-only lookups are hitting ~72% when canonicalized. There is some double-counting in how the replay was instrumented so numbers might shift slightly.
[00:48] Aisha Khan: When you say canonicalized, are you normalizing whitespace and punctuation, or are you running deeper template mapping?
[01:00] Nora Patel: Mostly whitespace, trimming, case-folding and a short tokenization normalization step before key generation. We can extend to template-level mapping but that will need rules from your product side.
[01:12] Ravi Menon: Hmm, we have a lot of small prompt variants — sometimes customers add micro-phrases. Curious if prefix caching with a 200 token prefix actually helps given our median prompt length is 90.
[01:24] Liam O'Connor: Good question. For your workload median at 90 tokens, prefix caching of 200 tokens will often include entire prompt plus some of response history. In practice, we saw the sweet spot at 100-150 tokens for similar customers. That boosts prefix hit-rate without bloating keys.
[01:36] Diego Ruiz: What's the eviction policy looked like, LRU? We noticed keys churn, TTLs were short in the initial run.
[01:42] Liam O'Connor: Right now pilot used LRU with a 12h default TTL, but effective TTL looked like 2-3h because working set exceeded fast cache size and items were evicted. We recommended increasing the on-disk cold cache and moving frequently touched prefixes into a pinned subset for test.
[02:00] Maya Chen: Quick note — the instrumentation glitch Liam mentioned: some of the earlier dumps conflated session affinity headers with prompt keys so KV counts were inflated. We'll send a cleaned CSV.
[02:12] Leah Park: There's also the prompt normalization question — if we aggressively normalize, do we risk losing semantic differences that matter for quality?
[02:20] Nora Patel: Yes, that's the tradeoff. Our suggested approach is staged: start conservative normalization (whitespace, case, common filler removal), measure quality delta with a small eval set, then iterate. We'll make it easy to roll back if you see regressions.
[02:35] Ravi Menon: Can you share the eval harness again? We want to run quality checks in CI after each config change.
[02:42] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely — we'll share the harness link. It includes A/B evaluation scripts and auto-metrics for perplexity + business metrics.
[02:50] Aisha Khan: About batching — we saw throughput improvements when batch size increased from 8 to 32, but latency got worse for single-user flows. Any guidance?
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: Classic trade. For your SLAs we suggest adaptive batching: route low-latency requests through a low-batch fast lane (batch size 1-4) and background or multiplexed workloads to higher batching. Redwood's runtime supports policy-based routing; we'll provide recommended policies based on your traffic shape.
[03:18] Diego Ruiz: Is that available on Dedicated or only in Hosted right now?
[03:24] Nora Patel: It's in both; on Dedicated you can pin kernels and assign GPU groups for the low-latency lane. On Private deployments, you'll need the routing config we provide and a small control-plane agent.
[03:36] Ravi Menon: Security question — for private deploys we need to show KMS usage and audit log retention. Do you have a short doc?
[03:44] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share an excerpt from our SOC2 packet and a KMS integration guide. Expect that in the next email.
[03:52] Leah Park: Great. Also, competitors question — some teams asked if Redis is faster for our use case.
[03:58] Liam O'Connor: Redis can be low-latency but lacks inference-aware prefix semantics and KV eviction tuned for tokenized keys. Pinecone is more vector-search oriented; not a direct replacement for token-level prefix caching. We'll outline tradeoffs in the config doc.
[04:12] Ravi Menon: On the numbers side, could you walk through the day-by-day hit rate variation — weekend vs weekday?
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: Sure — hit-rate dipped to ~38% on Monday because of a marketing campaign that injected many new prompts; weekdays stabilize ~50-60%, weekends slightly higher because traffic is more repetitive. We'll annotate the CSV with traffic labels.
[04:30] Aisha Khan: For the canonicalization rules, can we run a small model-level QA to ensure no quality regression? Maybe 500 samples?
[04:38] Nora Patel: Yes, 500 is fine for an initial check. We'll set that up and push results to the shared sheet.
[04:45] Diego Ruiz: Any recommendations for monitoring — specific SLOs we should set for cache hit-rate and tail latency?
[04:52] Liam O'Connor: For your product I'd recommend target KV hit-rate >60% with prefix reuse >70% and 99th percentile latency below 350ms for the low-latency lane. For background workloads acceptable 99p up to 700ms depending on SLAs.
[05:08] Maya Chen: Recap and next steps — we'll provide tuned configs, the eval harness, and the SOC2/KMS excerpt. Cinder will run the 48 hour replay with the configs and share logs. SE bench will run week of 2/16.
[05:20] Ravi Menon: Sounds good. One last small thing — is there a quick change we can do to increase prefix hit-rate without touching prompts? Maybe increase pinned set?
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: You can pin top 5% keys by frequency in the fast cache — that required a small config change and no prompt edits. We'll include commands in the spreadsheet.
[05:36] Aisha Khan: Ok thanks. If we see quality drift after canonicalization, we'll flag it in the ticket.
[05:42] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll follow up with the artifacts and book the deep benchmark. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
